decision.summary: The Federal Reserve voted to keep its benchmark interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Conditions in financial markets have generally improved in recent months.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this note to acknowledge that parts of the financial system are healing compared to earlier months.

changes.quote: Businesses are cutting back on fixed investment and staffing but appear to be making progress in bringing inventory stocks into better alignment with sales.
changes.explanation: This new line shows that while firms are still trimming staff and spending, they are successfully clearing out unsold goods.

changes.quote: The prices of energy and other commodities have risen of late.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted that certain commodity prices are starting to creep back up.

changes.quote: However, substantial resource slack is likely to dampen cost pressures, and the Committee expects that inflation will remain subdued for some time.
changes.explanation: Despite rising commodity prices, widespread economic slack keeps overall inflation pressures low.

changes.quote: The Federal Reserve is monitoring the size and composition of its balance sheet and will make adjustments to its credit and liquidity programs as warranted.
changes.explanation: The Fed added a reminder that it watches its massive asset holdings and emergency programs closely as conditions change.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in April suggests that the pace of economic contraction is slowing.

Although economic activity is likely to remain weak for a time, the Committee continues to anticipate that policy actions to stabilize financial markets and institutions, fiscal and monetary stimulus, and market forces will contribute to a gradual resumption of sustainable economic growth in a context of price stability.

The Committee will maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and continues to anticipate that economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for an extended period.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.97% APR costs about $54.04 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.72% and moved +7 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.59% would rise by about $13.26 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 9.4%, and employers added an average of -617k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was -1% over the past year (May 2009); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 0.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -4.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +5 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.29% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed intends to keep borrowing costs exceptionally low for an extended period to support the recovery. For educational purposes, an econometric forecast estimates the next meeting has a 35% chance of a hold and a 65% chance of a cut.
